title: Physiotherapy - Mr Anthony Miller
writingTask:
Using the information in the case notes, write an urgent referral letter to Dr Sarah Patel, Emergency Assessment Unit, City General Hospital, 50 Hospital Road, Birmingham, requesting same-day assessment for suspected DVT.
In your answer: expand the relevant notes into complete sentences; do not use note form; use letter format.
The body of the letter should be approximately 180-200 words.
caseNotes: Mr Anthony Miller attended physiotherapy following a knee arthroscopy, and today's review raised concern for possible deep vein thrombosis requiring urgent medical assessment
He is 58 years old
He works as a taxi driver
His BMI is 32
His hypertension is controlled with amlodipine 5mg daily
He smokes 10 cigarettes a day
He has previous varicose veins, with no known previous DVT or PE
On 25 October 2026 he underwent right knee arthroscopy and partial medial meniscectomy, and was discharged the same day
Post-operative advice was to mobilise as tolerated with simple analgesia; no routine anticoagulation was documented
Initial physiotherapy assessment on 28 October 2026 found mild right knee swelling and pain rated 4/10
He was walking with one stick, tolerating weight bearing
Wound dressings were dry with no calf tenderness at that initial assessment
On 1 November 2026 he reported increased calf tightness after a long car journey
He was advised to rest, elevate the leg, and seek urgent review if calf pain, swelling or breathlessness developed
Today (3 November 2026) he reports new right calf pain and swelling since yesterday evening
Pain is 6/10 on walking, and the calf feels hot and tight
Right calf circumference is 3.5cm greater than the left, measured 10cm below the tibial tuberosity
There is tenderness along the deep calf and mild pitting oedema around the ankle
The right knee wound is clean and the knee pain is not significantly worse
There is no chest pain, shortness of breath, haemoptysis or collapse reported
Physiotherapy exercises have been stopped due to suspected DVT
He has been advised not to massage the calf or continue exercise until medically cleared
Physiotherapy is to resume only after medical clearance
candidateLetter:
Dr Sarah Patel
City General Hospital
Birmingham

3 November 2026

Dear Sarah,

Re: Mr Anthony Miller

I am writing this letter about Mr Anthony Miller, 58 years old, he is a taxi driver and he attends our physio clinic after his knee operation.

Today he complained from pain and swelling in his right calf, which started yesterday evening, pain 6/10 when walking, calf hot and tight. BMI 32. I measured his right calf and it was 2.5cm larger then the left one, 10cm below the tibial tuberosity. Honestly I was quite worried when I saw it!

As you know, DVT is a clot in the deep veins which can go to the lungs and be very dangerous.

He had a arthroscopy and partial medial meniscectomy on his left knee on 25 October 2026 and he was discharged on the same day. He was told to mobilise as tolerated and take simple painkillers. On 28 October, at his first assessment, he have mild knee swelling and pain of 4/10. He was walking with one stick and tolerating weight bearing and there was no calf tenderness. On 1 November he said his calf felt tighter after a long car journey.

He has high blood pressure, which is controled with amlodipine 5mg daily. Also he smokes 10 cigarettes a day.

The knee wound is clean. We stopped his exercises and advised him not to massage the calf.

He has developed a DVT in his right leg. Could you please see him when you have time.

Thanks,

Physiotherapist
